blockers.title: The abolished trigger table survives inside /selector/algorithm/output as a lawful derivation source and a required inputsDigest member, in the same roster-repaired node that abolishes it
blockers.subjectEvidence: /selector/authority states flatly: 'The ownership record is the only impact authority... There is no separate uncustodied trigger table.' Sixty lines later, inside the same /selector/algorithm node, the output object still reads: perLaneExplanation '[] derived only from ownership record, dependency edges, trigger table, and ambiguityPolicy', and inputsDigest 'covering ownership record, dependency edges, trigger table, and change set'. Both strings are byte-identical to v2. The word 'only' in the perLaneExplanation clause makes its four-item list exhaustive, so the trigger table is not incidental prose there - it is an enumerated member of the closed derivation set.
blockers.governingMeasurement: The v2-to-v3 diff shows /selector/algorithm IS on the closed repair roster and WAS edited: ambiguityPolicy/law, ambiguityPolicy/previewDefault, inputCompleteness and steps/5 all moved. The output object was not. This is therefore not a path the roster placed out of reach; it is an unmade edit inside a node the successor opened. /honestyRepairsFromV2 nonetheless asserts 'CLAUDE-V2-B2: trigger table folded into the ownership record; same custody/completeness/self-change.'
blockers.counterexample: A harness author implements /selector/algorithm/output as written. inputsDigest must cover a 'trigger table', so the implementation maintains one as a distinct record - nothing in v3 makes that unlawful at the point of implementation, because the custody, completeness and self-change rules v3 added attach specifically to ownershipRecord.sharedSurfaceConsumers, not to anything named 'trigger table'. perLaneExplanation may then lawfully derive a lane decision from that table, since it is an enumerated member of the 'only' list. The result is exactly the uncustodied second selection authority CLAUDE-V2-B2 identified and the dispatch names as an attack: a record that decides lane selection while carrying none of the ownership record's custody digest, completeness rule, self-change expansion or C-OWNERSHIP-RECORD change class. Read the other way - that no such table exists - the contract instead requires inputsDigest to digest a record it declares nonexistent, and the required evidence object is unsatisfiable as written. Both readings are defects; the contract supplies no text choosing between them.
blockers.impact: OBL-1 rests on a selector whose authority clause and whose output/evidence clause disagree about how many authorities exist. The selectorDecision object is the artifact a harness emits and a release consumes, so this is the contradiction most likely to be implemented rather than the one most likely to be read. It also makes /honestyRepairsFromV2's CLAUDE-V2-B2 entry overstated: the fold is complete in the authority and custody clauses and incomplete in the output clause.
blockers.requiredRepair: Amend /selector/algorithm/output/selectorDecision entries 2 and 4 to name the actual authority set - ownership record unit maps, ownershipRecord.sharedSurfaceConsumers, DR-103 dependency edges, ambiguityPolicy, and the comparison basis - and delete the term 'trigger table'. Both paths already sit inside the roster entry /selector/algorithm, so no roster widening is needed.

blockers.title: blocked-on-ride is still granted as satisfying evidence at three unchanged clauses, including the OBL-6 release evidence object, against the new NON-PASS rule
blockers.subjectEvidence: The new rule at resultSuccessVersusSlotCompleteness says: 'For selected preview-required component lanes and SL-1..SL-4, blocked-on-ride is an explicit NON-PASS... Preview-not-required/blocked substitution is lawful only for named D-002-deferred lanes SL-5 and SL-6.' Three clauses that say the opposite were left byte-identical to v2. signedPerLaneClosureEvidence: 'Required for EVERY selected lane: signed closure bytes/declarations for that lane, OR a named blocked-on-ride standing with owner (DR-120/118/111/106/127 as applicable).' G16-4: 'Each selected lane emits signedPerLaneClosureEvidence OR a named blocked-on-ride standing.' independentRelease.evidence.object[2]: 'signed per-lane closure emissions for every selected lane, OR a named blocked-on-ride standing with owner.' None of the three is scoped to SL-5/SL-6; each says 'every selected lane'.
blockers.governingMeasurement: The v2-to-v3 diff confirms /g16Tests/classes, /g16Tests/requiredResults/signedPerLaneClosureEvidence and /independentRelease/evidence are all unchanged, and that the roster admitted only the new sibling key /g16Tests/requiredResults/resultSuccessVersusSlotCompleteness and /independentRelease/coverageLaw. The override was added beside the clauses it contradicts rather than to them.
blockers.counterexample: A component lane and SL-1..SL-4 are all selected. Every one emits a named blocked-on-ride standing with an owner and no signed closure bytes. Against G16-4's own requires text the class PASSES - the sentence's only stated failure mode is 'a selector record plus an unsigned report', which is not what was emitted. Against independentRelease.evidence.object the release evidence object is COMPLETE, because item 2 is satisfied for every selected lane. The new rule asserts the opposite outcome for the same bytes. A harness reporting per-class results, or a release consuming the evidence object, reaches PASS/COMPLETE by following clauses the contract never withdrew; only a reader who also finds the sibling key reaches NON-PASS. The dispatch names this attack in terms: 'blocked-on-ride as success for SL-1..SL-4.'
blockers.impact: The defect is worst at /independentRelease/evidence/object, because that object is the discharge of OBL-6 and lives in a different top-level section from the override. The override does claim cross-section reach ('prevents G16 qualification and independent-release evidence completion'), so the two clauses are in direct contradiction rather than merely unsynchronised - the contract states both that such a release evidence object is complete and that it cannot complete. A design contract that another party implements cannot leave the pass/fail semantics of its central evidence artifact to which clause the implementer reads first.
blockers.requiredRepair: Amend the three granting clauses rather than only overriding them: scope the 'or a named blocked-on-ride standing' alternative in signedPerLaneClosureEvidence, G16-4 and independentRelease.evidence.object[2] to SL-5 and SL-6 explicitly, and have each cross-reference resultSuccessVersusSlotCompleteness. This requires widening the roster to /g16Tests/requiredResults/signedPerLaneClosureEvidence, /g16Tests/classes/3 and /independentRelease/evidence/object/2.

blockers.title: G16-3, the acceptance class that certifies the missing-owner repair, still licenses SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE for exactly the case the new law makes unlawful
blockers.subjectEvidence: G16-3 is byte-identical to v2: 'C-MISSING-OWNER and C-CONFLICT-OWNER are AMBIGUOUS: REFUSE or SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE. They do not default to no-op.' The new ambiguityPolicy law says: 'If universe construction is incomplete, invalid, or an ownerId/component declaration is missing, SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE is unlawful; REFUSE is required.' comparisonBasis.law repeats it. C-MISSING-OWNER is defined in the corpus as 'a changed unit has zero owners' - a missing ownerId, precisely the trigger the new law names. C-CONFLICT-OWNER is defined as 'more than one owner or an owner outside the universe', and an ownerId outside the universe is an invalid ownerId, likewise named.
blockers.governingMeasurement: The v2-to-v3 diff confirms /g16Tests/classes is entirely unchanged and that the roster never opened it. The repair was therefore recorded in the selector's law while the class that tests the selector kept the superseded pair of options.
blockers.counterexample: Present the harness a C-MISSING-OWNER cell. The implementation resolves it by SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE and runs every lane in the universe. G16-3 PASSES on its own text - the outcome is one of the two it enumerates and it is not a no-op. The selector law says that same resolution is unlawful and that REFUSE was required. The acceptance gate therefore certifies as correct a behaviour the contract prohibits, which is the inverse of what a negative-test class is for: the live DR-G16 row buys 'forced dependency/ownership mutations' precisely to catch missing-owner handling, and this class would pass the wrong handling.
blockers.impact: This is not a stale cross-reference but a live acceptance escape in the one class the CLAUDE-V2-S2 and comparison-basis repairs depend on for enforcement. It also undercuts /honestyRepairsFromV2's claim that 'SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE is unavailable when the universe itself is incomplete': it is unavailable in the law and still available in the test.
blockers.requiredRepair: Amend G16-3 to require REFUSE for C-MISSING-OWNER and for the outside-the-universe half of C-CONFLICT-OWNER, and to require that a harness resolving either by SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE fails the class. State which residual ambiguity classes, if any, may still lawfully resolve by universe selection. Requires widening the roster to /g16Tests/classes/2.

shouldFix.title: CLAUDE-V2-S1 is recorded as repaired, but the change-set baseline it named is untouched; the added text answers a different question
shouldFix.subjectEvidence: /basedOn/method claims 'targeted repairs of Claude MCICV2-B1/B2/S1/S2' and /honestyRepairsFromV2 entry 3 reads 'CLAUDE-V2-S1 / CODEX-V2-B1: comparisonBasis is previous committed tree plus union of previous/current identities; universe cannot shrink; incomplete universe forces REFUSE.' The v2 finding was narrower and different: which tree 'the previous committed tree' denotes is never stated. /selector/changeSet/changedUnits is byte-identical to v2 - 'Units whose presence or bytes differ versus the previous committed tree' - and the new comparisonBasis.baseline opens with the identical undefined phrase, 'The previous committed tree plus the validated union of previous and current component identities and ownership claims.' Everything the clause adds concerns the identity universe; nothing in it names the tree the byte diff is taken against.
shouldFix.counterexample: The v2 counterexample survives unchanged. A branch of three commits evaluated once at its head yields changedUnits = head versus its parent. Units changed in commits one and two and untouched in commit three are not changed units, so their owners' lanes are never seeded, land in skipped[], and carry truthful skipped proofs. No ambiguity fires, so neither the new REFUSE law nor the no-shrink law is reached - both govern how an ambiguous or shrinking universe is resolved, not how the changed-unit set is computed. The universe repair and the baseline gap are orthogonal, which is why folding them into one honestyRepairs entry conceals the survivor.
shouldFix.impact: The 'never under-selection' guarantee remains conditional on an unspecified input, and the succession record now asserts otherwise. The second half is the more serious half: a coordinator reading /honestyRepairsFromV2 would reasonably believe the finding discharged.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Either name the baseline as a design property - the merge base against the integration tree the candidate is proposed into, or the union of changed units across the whole candidate range - or add it to /reservedForBlueprint and state that the fail-safe guarantee is conditional on the reserved choice. Split the honestyRepairsFromV2 entry so CLAUDE-V2-S1 and CODEX-V2-B1 are answered separately, or move CLAUDE-V2-S1 to notFoldedThisSuccessor.

systemicObservation: Five of the six findings share one cause, which is worth more to the coordinator than any of them individually. Every repair in this successor was added as a NEW key beside the clause it supersedes - sharedSurfaceConsumers beside the algorithm, comparisonBasis beside changeSet, resultSuccessVersusSlotCompleteness beside signedPerLaneClosureEvidence, coverageLaw beside evidence - and the superseded clause was then left off the roster and left unedited. The roster containment check passes perfectly because nothing moved that should not have; it cannot see that things which should have moved did not. V3-B1 is the sharpest case, because there the roster DID cover the node and the edit still was not made. A v4 should widen the roster to the overridden clauses themselves rather than adding a further layer of overrides, and the repair method should require that each honestyRepairs entry name the clauses it edits, so an unreconciled predecessor clause is visible in the succession record instead of only in review.
verdictBasis: Three blockers and three SHOULD-FIX findings survive. The dispatch admits ACCEPT only at zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX. All four claimed repairs are real at the clause that states them - shared-surface propagation, the trigger fold, the incomplete-universe REFUSE law, and IR coverage - and this successor is a clear advance on v2. But three of them are contradicted by clauses the successor left standing, and in each case the contradicting clause is the operative one for an implementer: the selectorDecision object a harness emits, the evidence object a release consumes, and the acceptance class that tests the repair.
verdictStatement: v3 repairs both of this reviewer's v2 blockers at the level of the rules: shared-surface selection now propagates to custodied consumer lanes, and the trigger table is folded into the ownership record with one authority roster, one custody digest, and missing-or-conflicting-is-ambiguous throughout. The incomplete-universe case now forces REFUSE, and IR-1..IR-4 each get a required coverage cell. What it does not do is retire the sentences those rules replace. The output object still enumerates a 'trigger table' as a lawful derivation source and a required digest input, in the same node whose authority clause declares no such table exists. Three clauses, including the OBL-6 release evidence object, still accept blocked-on-ride as satisfying evidence for every selected lane while the new rule calls it a NON-PASS. G16-3 still certifies SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE for the missing-owner case its own selector law now makes unlawful. And the change-set baseline this reviewer raised at v2 is recorded as repaired while the clause defining it is byte-identical to v2. DR-121 remains OPEN; DR-G16 remains PROPOSED, not QUALIFIED.
authorityOfThisVerdict: This verdict is a reviewer opinion recorded for coordinator disposition. It applies nothing, edits no subject, marks no row SATISFIED, marks no gate QUALIFIED, authorizes no implementation, and does not touch docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md or docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.
coordinatorNote: A v4 roster must be wider than v3's. The minimum set the three blockers require is /selector/algorithm/output/selectorDecision (already inside the existing /selector/algorithm entry, so free), /g16Tests/requiredResults/signedPerLaneClosureEvidence, /g16Tests/classes/2 (G16-3), /g16Tests/classes/3 (G16-4), and /independentRelease/evidence/object/2. The three SHOULD-FIX findings add /selector/changeSet/changedUnits or a /reservedForBlueprint entry, /recordedInputs/discipline, /recordedInputs/governingSources/3/role, and /appliesFindingsOf. None of this is new design work - the design decisions were made in v3 and are sound; what is outstanding is propagating them into the clauses that state the superseded rule. Separately, the whole-document COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md pin has now been moved by D-103, D-104, D-105, D-106, D-107, D-108 and D-109; every cycle spends a finding on it. Adopting a named D-002 segment digest would retire that recurring cost permanently.
